prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1112; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Police report received and reviewed. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the incident. Scene photos were submitted by the insured and show damage consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 3: Adjuster inspected the vehicle and found damage that matches the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records. Nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Attorney letter received with the claimant's written statement of the collision. The statement describes the sequence of events and the position of both vehicles. No independent witnesses have come forward to date.

Entry 5: Medical records received showing a shoulder injury. The reported injury fits the kind and force of the crash. Prior medical history reviewed, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Records show the claimant's symptoms improved steadily, and treatment tapered off as recovery progressed.

Entry 7: Claimant provided a supplemental statement through counsel adding a few minor details about the moments before impact. The core account of the collision remained the same as the original statement.

Entry 8: Photos submitted by the claimant were compared with the police report and the adjuster's inspection notes. They confirm some details of the scene, though they do not show the moment of impact.

Entry 9: Reviewed the medical bills against the treatment records. The charges line up with the care documented and the recovery timeline described by the treating provider.

Entry 10: Claim file reviewed and ready for the next step in the evaluation. Coverage confirmed for the driver named on the policy. Next action is to finalize the injury assessment with counsel.
